poster.title: Sahaj Path
poster.bookOrigin: Bengali educational writing by Rabindranath Tagore in the Santiniketan/Visva-Bharati context of Bengal, then British India.
poster.creator: Nandalal Bose (attributed)
poster.alt: A monochrome Bengali outer design with huge outlined title letters over horizontal white dashes, a tall branching tree below, thin ruled panels and small part and author wording at the foot.
poster.blurb: White branches and outlined Bengali letters animate a black-and-white page.

notes.title: The displayed edition
notes.body: Bichitra catalogue: Bengali Part I, 1337/1930. The illustrated outer design is page 6, preceding a separate title and imprint leaf. Exact wrapper terminology and cover attribution remain qualified.

notes.title: Writing and image-making
notes.body: A scholarly cover-history review attributes the 1930 cover and illustrations to Bose. The primary NGMA journal supports his Sahaj Path illustrations but does not separately identify this outer tree design.

notes.title: A visible design relationship
notes.body: The wide title panel gives way to a narrow tree. Straight rules organise the two organic forms while white side panels provide a pause.

poster.credit: A scholarly cover-history review attributes the 1930 cover and illustrations to Bose. The primary NGMA journal supports his Sahaj Path illustrations but does not separately identify this outer tree design.

studyData.intro: Large Bengali letters and a branching tree share a ruled monochrome page. This illustrated outer design survives in Bichitra’s 1930 Part I scan. Its exact wrapper status and the separate cover-artist attribution remain qualified.

regions.label: Large Bengali forms fill the upper panel
regions.summary: The large title forms occupy nearly the whole dark upper panel.

sections.heading: Visible in the cover
sections.body: The large title forms occupy nearly the whole dark upper panel. Broad black bodies are separated from the busy surrounding field by white outlines.

sections.heading: A possible reading
sections.body: The title is both readable language and a dominant image. Its broad curves can be compared with the branching structure below without equating writing with a picture.

sections.heading: A primer’s Bengali title
sections.body: সহজ পাঠ is read Sahaj Path and refers to easy or simple reading. The selected transcript gives the main title and small part and author wording; it does not reproduce the whole book’s educational text.
sections.translation: Sahaj Path; easy or simple reading

regions.question: What do you notice first in the title: words, curves or the contrast of black and white?

regions.label: White contours keep letters distinct
regions.summary: White contours follow the large black title bodies.

sections.heading: Visible in the cover
sections.body: White contours follow the large black title bodies. These continuous edges remain different from the short horizontal white marks outside the letters.

sections.heading: A possible reading
sections.body: The outlines let the title stay legible inside a patterned field. Their continuity matters as much as their colour because the surrounding pattern uses white too.

regions.question: How do you distinguish a letter outline from the surrounding white dashes?

regions.label: Short marks make a dense field
regions.summary: Short pale horizontal dashes repeat across the dark title panel.

sections.heading: Visible in the cover
sections.body: Short pale horizontal dashes repeat across the dark title panel. Their lengths and spacing vary around the much larger lettering.

sections.heading: A possible reading
sections.body: The small repeated marks establish a background rhythm. The title interrupts that rhythm with larger connected forms rather than relying on a new colour.

regions.question: Why do the letters remain dominant even though the pattern covers so much area?

regions.label: A narrow tree follows a wide title
regions.summary: A tall dark tree stands below the wide title panel.

sections.heading: Visible in the cover
sections.body: A tall dark tree stands below the wide title panel. Its canopy has many rounded lobes around a white branching interior.

sections.heading: A possible reading
sections.body: The change from a wide upper block to a narrow vertical tree creates a clear second movement. The tree can anchor the page without matching the title’s width.

regions.question: How does the narrow tree balance the much wider panel above it?

regions.label: White makes the branching structure
regions.summary: White lines divide and turn inside the dark tree canopy.

sections.heading: Visible in the cover
sections.body: White lines divide and turn inside the dark tree canopy. They thicken near the lower centre and narrow as they reach smaller branches.

sections.heading: A possible reading
sections.body: The light interior makes a tree readable within an almost solid dark silhouette. It shows how a pale absence can do descriptive work usually assigned to a dark line.

regions.question: Would the tree remain as clear if the white branches were filled with black?

regions.label: The canopy reaches the ground
regions.summary: A narrower trunk and small dark ground marks continue below the canopy.

sections.heading: Visible in the cover
sections.body: A narrower trunk and small dark ground marks continue below the canopy. The tree does not end as a detached floating crown.

sections.heading: A possible reading
sections.body: The taper from canopy to trunk gives the form a coherent structure. Its grounded base can make the straight surrounding rules feel like a setting rather than a cage.

regions.question: Which small marks most clearly make the tree feel planted?

regions.label: Straight rules organise organic forms
regions.summary: Thin straight rules enclose the page and divide the lower area into narrow panels.

sections.heading: Visible in the cover
sections.body: Thin straight rules enclose the page and divide the lower area into narrow panels. Their slight skew follows the scanned physical sheet.

sections.heading: A possible reading
sections.body: The rectilinear structure gives order to the curving letters and irregular canopy. The two systems remain distinct while sharing the same black-and-white vocabulary.

regions.question: Where is the contrast between straight rule and organic curve strongest?

regions.label: White side areas provide a pause
regions.summary: Large pale panels remain on either side of the central tree.

sections.heading: Visible in the cover
sections.body: Large pale panels remain on either side of the central tree. They contain far fewer marks than the dense title field above.

sections.heading: A possible reading
sections.body: These quieter areas let the tree retain a readable silhouette. They also slow the eye after the crowded upper panel, creating a different pace of looking.

regions.question: How would the tree change if the side panels repeated the title’s dense pattern?

regions.label: A small label identifies the part
regions.summary: Small Bengali wording appears in the lower left panel beneath the tree’s height.

sections.heading: Visible in the cover
sections.body: Small Bengali wording appears in the lower left panel beneath the tree’s height. It is separated from the large title by both space and a change of scale.

sections.heading: A possible reading
sections.body: The label provides an organisational cue without disturbing the dominant forms. Its smallness makes a practical detail part of a second, closer reading.

sections.heading: The displayed leaf and its limits
sections.body: Bichitra catalogues this Bengali Part I volume as 1337, corresponding to 1930. The illustrated outer design is scan page 6, before a separate title and imprint leaf. The monochrome scan establishes the forms shown here, but cannot establish the original paper or ink colours.

regions.question: What kind of information belongs in this quiet corner rather than the large title panel?

regions.label: The writer’s name near the foot
regions.summary: Rabindranath Tagore’s name is printed in a small Bengali line at the lower right.

sections.heading: Visible in the cover
sections.body: Rabindranath Tagore’s name is printed in a small Bengali line at the lower right. It balances the shorter part wording across the base.

sections.heading: A possible reading
sections.body: The paired small lines make a quiet footer below the visual drama. Their positions help complete the page while leaving the tree as the lower pictorial focus.

sections.heading: Writing, illustration and a qualified attribution
sections.body: Tagore wrote Sahaj Path. The NGMA journal documents Nandalal Bose’s illustrations for the work; a scholarly cover-history review also attributes the 1930 cover to him. Because the primary journal does not individually identify this outer design, the cover attribution remains qualified here.

sources.title: NGMA Art Journal: Nandalal Bose and Sahaj Path
sources.summary: The May–July 2022 issue discusses Bose’s Sahaj Path illustrations, their 1929–30 development and 1930 publication; it does not separately identify this tree outer design.

sources.title: Parabaas: a scholarly cover-history review
sources.summary: Discusses Bengali cover history and attributes the 1930 Sahaj Path cover and illustrations to Bose, citing Sombrata Sarkar’s study.

rows.meaning: Sahaj Path; an easy or simple reading primer.

connections.label: Branching forms
connections.title: Letters and wood
connections.text: The large curves of Bengali lettering and the white tree branches both turn and divide.

connections.label: Two rhythms
connections.title: A tree between rules
connections.text: The tree’s irregular silhouette sits within a straight ruled framework.
